claims.text: High-resolution inelastic neutron scattering can capture the phonon density of states of HfNbTaTiZr.
THz time-domain spectroscopy can measure the low-frequency electronic conduction of HfNbTaTiZr.
Combining INS and THz-TDS enables separate quantification of lattice and electronic thermal conductivity.
The proposed model will predict each thermal-transport channel within 10–15% error.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic contributions follow distinct temperature-dependent trends.
Between 300 and 1200 K, the summed lattice and electronic prediction will fall within 10–17 W/(K·m).
Spark plasma sintering can produce high-density HfNbTaTiZr with a controlled microstructure and minimal oxygen contamination.
INS-derived phonon density of states is an adequate mediator for predicting the lattice thermal-conductivity channel.
THz-TDS-derived electronic relaxation times are an adequate mediator for predicting the electronic thermal-conductivity channel.
Spectral deconvolution, potentially supplemented by time-resolved measurements, can clearly separate phonon and electronic contributions.
Treating the two transport channels separately avoids conflation through a shared Debye temperature.
Existing analytical models conflate lattice and electronic transport through Debye-temperature approaches.
Existing analytical models have prediction errors larger than 10–15%.
The proposed approach is applicable to high-purity, fully dense HfNbTaTiZr specimens with minimal oxygen contamination.
Significant extrinsic defect populations may prevent direct extension of the model to other HfNbTaTiZr samples.
Insufficient resolution of overlapping spectral features will reduce the model's predictive accuracy.
The lattice and electronic thermal conductivities can be independently derived from the proposed INS and THz-TDS measurements.

contradictions.description: The model is restricted to high-purity specimens with minimal oxygen, but its high-temperature target of 10–17 W/(K·m) comes from a specimen described in the query as containing 1 wt.% oxygen. The hypothesis does not justify transferring that benchmark to its stated sample class.

The mechanism says deconvolution techniques ensure clear separation, whereas the uncertainty field states that complete separation may not be achievable and may require further refinement. The former is overly definitive relative to the latter.
